response.overview: A traveler in a convertible drives through the countryside; the car breaks down—the engine makes popping noises—but it manages to reach the nearest village. A tow truck is called to collect the vehicle. Mechanics remove a damaged piston, attributing the failure to poor-quality engine oil and recommending Shell motor oil instead. They explain that Germany must import a large portion of its crude oil, which is then processed domestically. A map of Germany—shown with its 1918 borders (excluding Alsace-Lorraine)—highlights the cities where Shell operates production facilities: Hamburg, Wilhelmsburg, Harburg, Freital, Regensburg, Monheim, and Reisholz.
